a: High-entropy secret created by the client for PKCE.
Usually S256(hash of verifier) sent in the authorize request.
Stops attackers who intercept the auth code from exchanging it.
SPAs and mobile apps cannot keep client secrets; use PKCE.
Without PKCE, stolen redirect codes can be redeemed by attackers.
Use both state (CSRF) and PKCE (code theft) together.
Token request includes the original code_verifier.
plain method is weaker; prefer S256.
Use claimed HTTPS app links / universal links for redirects.
Rotate refresh tokens and detect reuse.
